site.title: Brook & Lathe
site.tagline: Furniture made to order in Hebden Bridge

posts.title: Reading tables for Todmorden library
posts.excerpt: Eight cherry tables for the reference room, built to outlast the schoolchildren.

posts.title: Twelve Calder chairs for a learning studio
posts.excerpt: A run of twelve chairs in oak, for a gallery education room in Wakefield.
posts.content: The learning team wanted chairs that children and adults could both use, and that could be stacked two high on a trolley. We lowered the Calder seat to 430 mm and added a back rail you can grip.

posts.title: A writing desk for a flat in Leeds
posts.excerpt: The Aire desk, made 150 mm narrower to fit between two windows.
posts.content: The client measured the gap between the windows three times before she wrote to us. The desk is 850 mm wide, in cherry, with one drawer lined in undyed felt.

posts.title: The Crag bench, a run of thirty
posts.excerpt: Larch benches for footpaths on the moor above Heptonstall.
posts.content: Thirty benches in Kielder larch for Pennine Prospects, left unfinished so they weather silver. Each one has the grid reference of where it sits cut into the end.

posts.title: A court cupboard in fumed oak
posts.excerpt: A cupboard for a farmhouse kitchen, darkened with ammonia to match the beams.
posts.content: Fuming takes two days in a sealed tent in the yard. The oak goes from honey to a deep brown and the carving shows up more than it did when pale.

posts.title: Rush-seated stools with Felicity Irons
posts.excerpt: We made the frames, Felicity wove the seats from Somerset rush.
posts.content: Forty stools over one summer. Felicity cut the rush on the River Ouse and wove the seats in her barn. The frames are ash with sycamore rails.
